Rassie VS Goliath

By: Graham Coetzer | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After a leaked video of South Africa's Director of Rugby Rassie Erasmus criticising an international referee went viral, he and the SARU face a disciplinary hearing with World Rugby this weekend.

Unique Selling Point:
Erasmus took on Australian referee Nic Berry in a hour long video after the first test between the Springboks and the British and Irish Lions earlier this year in Cape Town. In the video, he questioned many of Berry's decisions, and notably, suggested that Berry treated Springboks skipper Siya Kolisi differently to British & Irish Lions counterpart Alun Wyn Jones. The issue for world rugby is not so much the contents of the video, but rather the fact that it leaked, which is a breach of their Code of Conduct. Erasmus has denied that he leaked the video, and according to some sources the video leaked social media site Vimeo from Australia, after it was sent to Nic Berry...

Summary:
Experts agree there is very little doubt that Erasmus would be found guilty according to the code if he is responsible for the leak. But its up to World Rugby to prove that. Erasmus and his lawyer Frikkie Erasmus are confident they will win the case, but have revealed nothing on their strategy to the media. But some of the issues raised by Erasmus in his video point to much bigger problems at World Rugby. The organisation is seen by many to be an "Old Boys Club", with outdated rules and regulations, which often favor them and not the game itself. Berry's condescending tone towards Kolisi during the match is but one example of this. Another is the seemingly absolute protection afforded to referees. International rugby involves hundreds of millions of rands, and decisions made by referees have massive impacts. And while coaches and players have to face the music in endless press conferences after a match, referees never have to. Official complaints against referees are handles behind closed doors, in internal hearings by the very same people who stand accused of running their own old buys club. So while Erasmus may or may not be found in breach of World Rugby's Code of Conduct, perhaps it is time for the organisation to ask itself some very difficult questions about fairness, equality and justice within it's ranks.

Further information:
Dario applied to World Rugby on our behalf for permission to film the virtual hearing, which was denied based on the fact that CB does not have Locus Standi to bring the application.

We have been in contact with Erasmus' lawyer, Frikkie Erasmus, who has been giving us a lot of info off the record.

According to sources, World Rugby has agreed that 23 of 26 complaints by Erasmus during his video rant were in fact accurate. (Although this will not impact the hearing)

While referees should and do enjoy some protection from criticism, the way things stand now there is very little transparency in the process, which could lead to much bigger issues like match fixing etc.

We will cover both points of view in regards to how referees should be treated etc

I have requested relevant footage from SuperSport on the match in question, Rassie general footage, rugby footage etc

Script:


Rassie Redcarded
First Draft Script
28 October 2021

Sound Up Rassie Erasmus Leaked Video
Rassie: And then ja, you know, if you think this was going over the top and this shouldn’t go out to the media, then I did this in my personal capacity, not as part of the Springboks, and I’ll withdraw myself from the Springbok management team… Thank you.

Voice
A visibly frustrated Rassie Erasmus, South Africa’s Director of Rugby and the man who led the Springboks to the Wolrd Cup Title in 2019. The clip you’ve just seen is an extract from a video that Erasmus made earlier this year, after the Springboks lost the first of three test matches against the British and Irish Lions. A series that’s only played once every twelve years.

Sound Up Supersport visuals
And the Lions celebrate an incredible second half come back…

Voice
The video went viral after it leaked onto social media, and caused a storm amongst the international rugby fraternity. During the 62 minute clip, Erasmus delivered a scathing analysis of the match officials performances, most of it directed at Australian referee Nic Berry.

Sound Up Rassie Erasmus Leaked Video
Its a difficult one to explain, how do you make a mistake like that?

Voice
Erasmus questioned no less than 26 decisions made during the game. A game he had first hand knowledge of as he controversially joined the team on field as the world’s best paid water-boy. One talking point in the video was Berry’s awarding of a penalty rather than a yellow card for this illegal spear tackle on Boks fullback Willie le Roux.

Sound Up Rassie Erasmus Leaked Video
Rassie: Here is obviously the big debate, which is mind baffling, if you look at the score, 19 -17 again, I haven’t seen one incident like this in the last 5 years where a player has got away with less than a yellow card here.

Voice
The furore around the video is more about it being leaked to the public than it’s content. For a senior member of a team to publicly criticise a referee is a serious no-no in the world of International Rugby. And the sport’s governing body, World Rugby, has since charged Erasmus and the South African Rugby Union with misconduct.

Link Bongani
Rugby is a serious game, there are so many people involved. From the coaches, to the psychologists, to the players, to the nutritionists, it is a multi billion rand industry and one bad decision, could up-end a career.

Voice
Veteran sports journalist Mark Keohane believes World Rugby would be better served addressing the underlying concerns raised by the Erasmus video than by targeting him.

Sound Up Mark Keohane
And whats happening with the Rassie Erasmus thing is, it’s like everyone is targeting the whistle blower, and they’re not looking at the message.

Voice
Last sunday, the Rapport newspaper said that behind the scenes, World Rugby allegedly agreed with 23 of the 26 concerns raised in the Erasmus video.

Sound Up Mark Keohane
Bongani: You cannot cast aspersions on the integrity,and the character and reputation of the referee. Isn’t that reasonable?

Mark: Their big thing is he should never of spoken out. The old boys club is under siege, and they should have been under siege a long time ago. And I’m sick and tired of reading this rhetoric of the referee is untouchable, you don’t go there. You do go there. The referee these days gets paid well, it’s his profession, his or hers.

Voice
In the video Erasmus also questioned why the South Africans were not awarded a possibly game winning penalty in the 71st minute for foul play on Springbok wing Makazole Mapimpi.

Sound Up Rassie Erasmus Leaked Video
Rassie: But here’s clearly the foul play part where Mapimpi gets drawn back. So irrelevant in my opinion if Cheslyn did knock the ball on or not, that should be in my opinion a penalty right in front of the poles.

Voice
The incident also led to Erasmus claiming that Springbok Captain Siya Kolisi was treated differently to his British and Irish Lions counterpart Alun Wyn Jones by match officials.

Sound Up Rassie Erasmus Leaked Video
Rassie: Now you’ll clearly see here there Alun Wyn Jones refers to the…and then Siya refers to holding back. And they just told Siya to go away, and Alun Wyn just stays there.And Siya had to walk away. Again I felt the respect shown to Siya compared to Alun Wyn was just two different levels.

Sound Up Xola Ntshinga
Bongani: And dismissing Siya Kolisi like that?

Xola: Yes, that I think is almost inexcusable.

Voice
Sports broadcaster Xola Ntshinga says seeing the World Cup winning captain and one of the most likeable characters in global rugby brushed off like that left a sour taste in his mouth.

Sound Up Xola
So to see Siya being summarily dismissed by the officials I think is very concerning. I do understand that in the heat of the moment and with everything happening and a decision needing to be made and players badgering you at the same time, it is very easy to get lost in the malaise and sort of, ok all the players go away, but he was talking to one captain, surely he should also speak to the other.

Voice
Matthew Williams is a former coach of the Scottish national team and provincial sides like New South Wales, and agrees with most of what Erasmus said in the video.

Sound Up Matthew Williams
Bongani: Matthew, does Rassie Erasmus have a point?

Matthew: The content of what Rassie put out I thought was very accurate. I thought the South Africans were hard done by.

Voice
But he’s also quick to point out that if Erasmus was responsible for the leak, he would be in breach of the governing body’s code of conduct, a charge that could see him and SA Rugby face reprimands, fines and even the forfeiture of a match.

Sound Up Matthew Williams
It’s the putting it out publicly, means that Rassie’s fallen foul of our code of conduct in the eyes of World Rugby.

Voice
Erasmus declined to comment until the matter was resolved, but his lawyer Frikkie Erasmus has previously said his defense would be that he was not responsible for leaking the video to the public. We spoke to Frikkie Erasmus late on thursday afternoon.

Sound Up Frikkie Erasmus
In terms of the specific instructions of the Chairman of the Tribunal, I unfortunately cannot comment on the disciplinary process against Rassie other then confirming that it will continue online on saturday and sunday.

Voice
Erasmus and the South African Rugby Union applied to World Rugby to have their virtual hearing open to the public, a request that was denied. Carte Blanche also asked to film the proceedings, but we had no better luck.

Link Bongani
Is there anything like being at the stadium, especially if you love the game. So we tried to reach out to World Rugby, but they told us we don’t have Locus Standi. They didn’t allow us to film the proceedings because we don’t have a direct interest in the matter. Try telling that to the fans - they don’t have a direct interest in the matter.

Voice
And perhaps it’s this rather archaic notion that everything needs to be kept behind closed doors that has some commentators fuming at the sport’s governing body.

Sound Up Mark Keohane
Bongani: You say that this is a temper tantrum by World Rugby?

Mark: Yeah, everyone said it was a temper tantrum from Rassie Erasmus, to me it’s very much the son who stands up to the father and says no more, why are we doing it like this? And it’s like you should be seen, you shouldn’t be heard and we’ll slap you and put you back in the corner.

Voice
Williams says the game in it’s current form has so many rules and regulations, we should have some sympathy for the referees trying to make sense of it all in the heat of the moment.

Sound Up Matt Williams
It’s as if the system is setup for them to fail. In NFL there are seven officials on the field, we have one official who has to make hundreds and hundreds of decisions in a game.

Voice
And that’s a sentiment echoed by Ntshinga.




Sound Up Xola
Not too many kids want to grow up to become referees. So attracting people to even take on the job is a massive challenge globally. So I understand why they want to have this layer of protection around them.

Link Bongani
But the question is, do the referees face the same consequences for mistakes as would the players and coaches, is it time for a change in World Rugby?

Voice
South African Rugby Union accredited agent Mark Greeff has represented the likes of Springbok scrum-half Faf de Klerk in the past. He’s seen the consequences of bad refereeing first hand.

Sound Up Mark Greeff
It can absolutely make or break a career you know, you go onto a senior level and you’re playing a serious game and your CEO or your sponsor have said to you look, you win this final and we’ll give you an extra three year contract, at a million rand a month and there we go. And you end up losing the game by one point because of a bad call maybe…

Sound Up Xola
The one thing that we know is coaches aren’t allowed to comment on referees, the media’s definitely discouraged from making comments or criticism’s about referees. Referees don’t face the press, they don’t do a post match press conference.

Sound Up Matt Williams
Officiating has been the biggest problem facing rugby for well over 15 years. And World Ruby’s refusal to reform, and I have to say the referees as a body’s refusal to reform is a huge problem. So you’ve got two issues there, you’ve got the legislation, the laws of the game, you’ve got far too many technical laws, scrums and so on, and games are being determined on their interpretation of technicalities.

Voice
Both the South African and World Rugby Unions have declined to comment until the legalities have run their course, but coincidence or not, after the video emerged, South Africa won the following matches to clinch the test series by two games to one.

Link Bongani
Brilliant coach, master tactician and strategist, but also controversial and somewhat of a maverick. So what does World Rugby do with Rassie Erasmus? Whatever the outcome of this case, if nothing else perhaps, he has started a conversation that’s long overdue.












Promos
Promo1 (21 sec)

Voice
In the high stakes game of international rugby, one bad decision from match officials could have dire consequences (7)

Sound Up Rassie Erasmus Leaked Video

Voice
But has Rassie Erasmus bitten off more then he can chew, as he faces a disciplinary hearing this weekend - after a video of him criticising match officials went viral?



Promo 2 (21 sec)

Voice
Voice
It’s Rassie Erasmus vs World rugby, the brilliant tactician and master strategist faces charges of misconduct from the sports governing body after he criticised international match officials.

Sound Up Mark Keohane
And I think what happened in the Lion’s series is that finally someone with standing, integrity and authority said enough is enough.

Voice
Is it time for a change in World Rugby?



Promo 3 (11 sec)
He’s known as a wily old fox, the world’s most well paid water-boy and South Africa’s director of rugby. will Rassie Erasmus survive charges of misconduct brought by World Rugby?

Voice And perhaps it’s this rather archaic notion that everything needs to be kept behind closed doors that has some commentators fuming at the sport’s governing body. Sound Up Mark Keohane Bongani: You say that this is a temper tantrum by World Rugby? Mark: Yeah, everyone said it was a temper tantrum from Rassie Erasmus, to me it’s very much the son who stands up to the father and says no more, why are we doing it like this? And it’s like you should be seen, you shouldn’t be heard and we’ll slap you and put you back in the corner. Voice Williams says the game in it’s current form has so many rules and regulations, we should have some sympathy for the referees trying to make sense of it all in the heat of the moment. Sound Up Matt Williams It’s as if the system is setup for them to fail. In NFL there are seven officials on the field, we have one official who has to make hundreds and hundreds of decisions in a game. Voice And that’s a sentiment echoed by Ntshinga. Sound Up Xola Not too many kids want to grow up to become referees. So attracting people to even take on the job is a massive challenge globally. So I understand why they want to have this layer of protection around them. Link Bongani But the question is, do the referees face the same consequences for mistakes as would the players and coaches, is it time for a change in World Rugby? Voice South African Rugby Union accredited agent Mark Greeff has represented the likes of Springbok scrum-half Faf de Klerk in the past. He’s seen the consequences of bad refereeing first hand. Sound Up Mark Greeff It can absolutely make or break a career you know, you go onto a senior level and you’re playing a serious game and your CEO or your sponsor have said to you look, you win this final and we’ll give you an extra three year contract, at a million rand a month and there we go. And you end up losing the game by one point because of a bad call maybe… Sound Up Xola The one thing that we know is coaches aren’t allowed to comment on referees, the media’s definitely discouraged from making comments or criticism’s about referees. Referees don’t face the press, they don’t do a post match press conference. Sound Up Matt Williams Officiating has been the biggest problem facing rugby for well over 15 years. And World Ruby’s refusal to reform, and I have to say the referees as a body’s refusal to reform is a huge problem. So you’ve got two issues there, you’ve got the legislation, the laws of the game, you’ve got far too many technical laws, scrums and so on, and games are being determined on their interpretation of technicalities. Voice Both the South African and World Rugby Unions have declined to comment until the legalities have run their course, but coincidence or not, after the video emerged, South Africa won the following matches to clinch the test series by two games to one. Link Bongani Brilliant coach, master tactician and strategist, but also controversial and somewhat of a maverick. So what does World Rugby do with Rassie Erasmus? Whatever the outcome of this case, if nothing else perhaps, he has started a conversation that’s long overdue. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): After a leaked video of South Africa's Director of Rugby Rassie Erasmus criticising an international referee went viral, he and the SARU face a disciplinary hearing with World Rugby this weekend.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Erasmus took on Australian referee Nic Berry in a hour long video after the first test between the Springboks and the British and Irish Lions earlier this year in Cape Town. In the video, he questioned many of Berry's decisions, and notably, suggested that Berry treated Springboks skipper Siya Kolisi differently to British & Irish Lions counterpart Alun Wyn Jones. The issue for world rugby is not so much the contents of the video, but rather the fact that it leaked, which is a breach of their Code of Conduct. Erasmus has denied that he leaked the video, and according to some sources the video leaked social media site Vimeo from Australia, after it was sent to Nic Berry...
metadata.Summary: Experts agree there is very little doubt that Erasmus would be found guilty according to the code if he is responsible for the leak. But its up to World Rugby to prove that. Erasmus and his lawyer Frikkie Erasmus are confident they will win the case, but have revealed nothing on their strategy to the media. But some of the issues raised by Erasmus in his video point to much bigger problems at World Rugby. The organisation is seen by many to be an "Old Boys Club", with outdated rules and regulations, which often favor them and not the game itself. Berry's condescending tone towards Kolisi during the match is but one example of this. Another is the seemingly absolute protection afforded to referees. International rugby involves hundreds of millions of rands, and decisions made by referees have massive impacts. And while coaches and players have to face the music in endless press conferences after a match, referees never have to. Official complaints against referees are handles behind closed doors, in internal hearings by the very same people who stand accused of running their own old buys club. So while Erasmus may or may not be found in breach of World Rugby's Code of Conduct, perhaps it is time for the organisation to ask itself some very difficult questions about fairness, equality and justice within it's ranks.
metadata.Further information: Dario applied to World Rugby on our behalf for permission to film the virtual hearing, which was denied based on the fact that CB does not have Locus Standi to bring the application. We have been in contact with Erasmus' lawyer, Frikkie Erasmus, who has been giving us a lot of info off the record. According to sources, World Rugby has agreed that 23 of 26 complaints by Erasmus during his video rant were in fact accurate. (Although this will not impact the hearing) While referees should and do enjoy some protection from criticism, the way things stand now there is very little transparency in the process, which could lead to much bigger issues like match fixing etc. We will cover both points of view in regards to how referees should be treated etc I have requested relevant footage from SuperSport on the match in question, Rassie general footage, rugby footage etc
